fixture: dagrun applet registry, read-only consumer classification
registry_format: urn:phenotype:atlas-plan:1:applet (one JSON file per advertisement, extension .json)
note: Measured, not reasoned. Paths are relative to this directory. Each case was produced by running the reader against the directory and recording what came back; see ../../../../../README.md for the replay commands and ~/CodeProjects/temp/dagrun-workboard-adapter.md for the consumer contract these pin down.

cases.input_state: a real advertisement captured from a live `dagrun serve`
cases.verify_outcome: reachable=false, error="...connection refused" once the captured serve is gone; reachable=true while a serve answers on 127.0.0.1:52391 with manifest id=dagrun and a non-empty version
cases.expected_adapter_state: OFFLINE (files exist, origin does not answer) or READY
cases.trap: the same bytes read as READY and as OFFLINE depending only on the probe moment, so the file is never evidence of liveness
pid 4 is a live kernel pid on every Unix host, so a pid-based liveness guess says UP and is wrong

cases.input_state: byte-identical copy of a valid record under a different filename
cases.verify_outcome: reachable=false; identical row emitted a second time
cases.trap: ReadInstances neither dedupes by id nor checks filename==id, so two rows appear and a naive consumer renders two servers

cases.input_state: id "not a valid id", which the schema pattern forbids
cases.trap: the id pattern is a publish-time rule (Validate), not a read-time rule, so readers must not trust id shape
reported in errors[], never as a row; a consumer that reads only instances[] cannot see it at all
decoding uses DisallowUnknownFields, so a later additive field makes every older dagrun machine read the record as garbage

cases.verify_outcome: unreadable: read_only is false; this surface has no write path, so a file claiming otherwise was not written by it
cases.trap: none: this one is an honest refusal, and its message explains itself
a writer killed mid-write leaves exactly this, and it is indistinguishable from corruption to a reader that only counts rows

cases.verify_outcome: ignored silently, not even in errors[]
cases.trap: silent, so an adapter cannot report it; do not glob *.json and assume the glob is the registry

process_cases.observed: instances=[], errors=[], pruned=[], rc=0; the directory is NOT created by the read
process_cases.trap: identical output to an empty registry and to an all-unreadable registry

process_cases.case: registry directory exists and is empty
process_cases.observed: instances=[], errors=[], rc=0; human mode prints only 'no dagrun servers advertised in <dir>'

process_cases.trap: rc=0; only errors[] separates BROKEN from EMPTY

process_cases.case: manifest answers 200 but declares another applet
process_cases.trap: a different program on the recorded port is detected, which is good, but the row still looks like a dagrun record

process_cases.case: manifest declares id=dagrun with no version
process_cases.trap: the probe requires id==dagrun AND a non-empty version; both must pass

process_cases.case: --prune on a registry with dead origins
process_cases.observed: pruned reports the instance IDs, not filenames: ["127.0.0.1_52391", "not a valid id", "127.0.0.1_52391"], files removed
process_cases.trap: prune deletes files and names them ambiguously when two records share an id; a read-only consumer must never call it

process_cases.observed: instances[], errors[], files on disk all unchanged
process_cases.trap: none: verify probes, it does not delete
